# Optimize the TOOL SURFACE — ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED fixes this iteration

## THE READER (who consumes what you edit)
At runtime these capabilities are read by `aws/gpt-oss-120b` — capability tier: **mid**. The reader is a mid-capability model (e.g. ~100B open weights). Be EXPLICIT: imperative step-by-step rules, at least one worked few-shot example per non-trivial behavior, short decision chains, and literal argument/slot-filling docs on every tool parameter. Lean HARD on deterministic tool-code enforcement — a behavioral rule it 'knows' but skips must be enforced in code, not restated in prose.
Optimize your edits for THIS reader's capability level, not for your own. When the reader is weaker than you, prefer explicit rules, worked examples, and code enforcement over terse prose you would personally infer.


Focus: every failing task on the val split. Current val reward 0.400: 1 solid / 6 flaky / 3 failing of 10 tasks.

## EMPTY SEED — create the capability from scratch
The capability directory is EMPTY (no pre-existing content). This is the first iteration starting from a blank slate. Your job is to CREATE the initial capability content — not edit existing files (there are none). Analyze the failing trajectories in `./trajectories/` to understand what the agent needs, then create the capability files from scratch (e.g. SKILL.md, prompt.txt, tools.json, policy.md — whatever the capability type requires). Read `./guidance/<cap>/SKILL.md` for the expected file format and structure. A good initial capability addresses the most common failure patterns visible in the trajectories.


GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself).

**The tool surface is the ONLY edit surface.** Your artifact is `tools/tools.py`: the
airline agent's 14 tools, with their real bodies. tau2's system prompt — the airline
policy — is NOT part of this capability: it is fixed, it reaches the agent exactly as the
benchmark ships it, and you cannot change it. So every fix you ship is a change to tool
CODE, tool DOCUMENTATION, or the SET of exposed tools. A cluster you would have fixed with
a prompt rule must instead be fixed in the tool that owns the action.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## PREFER CODE OVER DOCUMENTATION (this is where prior iterations fell short)
A strong iteration's `tools/tools.py` diff contains real CODE — guards, validations,
computations, new or changed tool bodies — across SEVERAL tools. The recurring failure
mode to avoid: an iteration that only rewords docstrings.
- **A BEHAVIORAL miss is NOT fixed by documentation.** When the agent already "knows" the
  rule but skips it (doesn't call `get_user_details` / `get_reservation_details` before
  acting, acts on a guess, re-asks after consent, miscomputes a total) — a longer docstring
  it will skim the same way does nothing. Enforce it in CODE: an in-body guard /
  validation / computation in the EXISTING tool, or a composite tool that performs the
  whole action. Documentation is reserved for genuine KNOWLEDGE gaps (a fact, format or
  criterion the agent cannot derive).
- **Do NOT defer a capability-gap cluster** ("would need a compute tool — next
  iteration"). If a cluster needs a compute / validation / composite tool, BUILD it THIS
  iteration — that is the highest-leverage edit available, not something to postpone.
So for each cluster, first ask "can this be enforced in the tool body?" — if yes, do that.

## The THREE TESTS every change must pass (this is the whole game)
Before you keep any edit, confirm all three. Drop any edit that fails even one.
1. **REAL** — it targets a cluster that is FAILING in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/`
   (reward 0, partial-credit, or communication/omission). Never edit for a hypothetical
   problem, never touch a path only used by already-PASSING tasks.
2. **SAFE (bounded blast radius)** — the real regression question is *behavioral*:
   **would this edit change what the agent DOES on ANY currently-passing task?** Not
   "does a passing task call this tool" — "does the agent now take a different action,
   or newly ACT where it correctly REFUSED / escalated". Two blast-radius classes:
   - **BOUNDED** — an in-body guard/computation that fires ONLY on the exact violating
     condition. Only already-failing inputs hit it; passing tasks are untouched by
     construction. This is the SAFE default — prefer it.
   - **UNBOUNDED** — any edit that changes a whole decision class: loosening a refusal a
     tool currently performs, widening what a tool will accept, removing a precondition,
     or dropping/replacing a primitive the agent uses on passing tasks. Allowed ONLY if
     the new behavior is correct for EVERY task in that class AND you have read the
     currently-passing tasks in the class and confirmed none relied on the old behavior.
     Otherwise encode the discriminating CONDITION instead (see the DECISION lever below).
   Name the passing tasks in each edit's blast-radius class and state which class it is.
   A regression wastes the whole candidate (the gate rejects a net-zero), not one task.
3. **VERIFIED** — you have shown it actually fixes its target (see VERIFY-THE-FIX). An
   edit you cannot verify is a guess — drop it.

Quality AND breadth: ship every fix that passes the three tests. The only edits to leave
out are the speculative ones, not real fixes you ran out of patience for. Don't re-add
anything `LEDGER.md` / `JOURNAL.md` show was already tried and rejected.

## Read these first (everything is in this working directory)
- **`./guidance/tools/SKILL.md` — READ IT IN FULL before you edit; it is the MENU of
  improvement TYPES available to you.** It lists the concrete kinds of change this
  capability allows: in-body validation guards, normalization, computation, composite /
  atomic-write tools, loop tools, discriminating-predicate guards, enriched return values
  and actionable errors, add/remove tools, sharpened names and descriptions. Do not invent
  change types from memory — take them from the skill, and deliberately apply MULTIPLE
  DIFFERENT types this iteration, matching each cluster to the strongest type the skill
  describes for it. Also read `./guidance/tools/references/optimizer-playbook.md`.
- **`./guidance/sources/data_model.py`** — tau2's airline data model (`FlightDB`,
  `Reservation`, `Passenger`, `Payment`, `Flight`, cabin/insurance enums). Your tool code
  imports these REAL types, so read them before writing code that touches reservations,
  payments or flight state. Code that guesses a field name will raise at runtime and cost
  the whole candidate.
- `./guidance/diagnose/SKILL.md` — the failure-clustering method. Use it.
- `./trajectories/` — see the section below; this is your ground truth.
- `./LEDGER.md` — FACTS (read-only): every prior iteration's outcome + the exact tasks it
  broke/fixed. Your SAFE test starts here — never re-introduce a change that broke a task.
- `./JOURNAL.md` — the accumulating handover. Each entry is the optimizer's INTENT, and
  directly below it the framework stamps a **RESULT** line (objective: ACCEPTED/REJECTED ·
  Δ · the exact tasks fixed/broke). The RESULT lines — not the intent — are the truth of
  what worked: read them all before proposing. If the most recent RESULT is **REJECTED**,
  its batch was reverted; read that entry's `./prior_iterations/<id>/diff.patch`, keep the
  edits that did NOT appear in its `broke={...}`, and DROP or REDESIGN the ones that did —
  do NOT resubmit the whole rejected batch, and do NOT abandon the cluster. APPEND your new
  entry (intent only) below the marker; never edit earlier entries or re-try a refuted idea.
- `./RUNMAP.md` + `./prior_iterations/<id>/` — EVERY prior iteration's (accepted AND
  rejected) PROCESS.md + diff.patch. Read the one(s) that touched a cluster you're about to
  work on, so you build on what worked and avoid repeating what regressed.
- `./PROCESS.md` — your REQUIRED explainability file for THIS iteration (template inside).
- `./guidance/optimizer/<name>.md` — your agent's subagent/parallelism features (optional).
- The benchmark / runner source is at `/home/skillberry/.cache/capevolve-ci/skillberry-benchmarks` — read-only context you may consult to understand tools, scoring, or task structure.

## THIS BENCHMARK: what the traces and the score actually are
- **`./trajectories/` holds one JSON per rollout** of the candidate you are forking from,
  named `<task>__<tag>__t<trial>.json`. Each is `{"input", "rollout", "score"}`:
  - `rollout.trace` (same as `rollout.output`) — the FULL transcript: the user simulator's
    turns, the agent's turns, every `tool_calls` entry **with its arguments**, and every
    tool result (`role: "tool"`). This is where you see what the agent actually did.
  - `rollout.metadata.tau2_reward` — tau2's reward for that rollout.
  - **`rollout.metadata.tau2_reward_info` — the per-check breakdown.** Keys: «redacted»
    (did the final database state match), `action_checks` (one per required action: which
    action, and `action_match`), `communicate_checks`, `nl_assertions`, `env_assertions`,
    plus `reward`, `reward_basis`, `reward_breakdown`. **USE IT to localize the exact
    defect: which action failed, and which ARGUMENT of it.**
  - `rollout.error` — non-null means the rollout did NOT complete for an infrastructure
    reason (a tau2 failure, or the documented user-simulator `###STOP###` artifact). Those
    are EXCLUDED from scoring and are NOT tool failures: do not optimize against them.
  - `score.feedback` — the argument-level signal derived from the above.
- **The score is tau2's own task reward in [0,1]** (`sim.reward_info.reward`, surfaced as
  `rollout.metadata.tau2_reward`) — required actions performed + information communicated.
  That exact recorded number is what the gate uses; nothing re-runs it.
- If a directory of tau2's NATIVE results files appears instead (a `Results` record with a
  `simulations` array), the same fields live at `simulations[i].messages` and
  `simulations[i].reward_info` — read them the same way.
- The FAILURES block at the end of this prompt summarizes the above; read the actual trace
  files for the clusters you'll fix, don't rely on the summary alone.
- An `action_checks` record also contains the EXPECTED action. Use it to identify the
  failing action and its argument KEYS, then write a fix that is GENERAL (see
  NON-OVERFITTING) — never a special case for the expected value you read there.

## Process (do this, then STOP)
**Parallelism:** Your agent supports parallel subagents/worktrees (see ./guidance/optimizer/claude-code.md). FAN OUT to cover MANY clusters at once: one read-only subagent per trajectory-group to diagnose, then one edit-subagent per issue (each in its own worktree), then MERGE every edit into this ONE candidate with no conflicts. This is how a single iteration fixes many issues across many trajectories, not just the biggest one.
1. Read `./guidance/tools/SKILL.md` + `./guidance/sources/data_model.py` + the diagnose
   method + the cross-iteration files (LEDGER facts, JOURNAL handover, RUNMAP).
2. Diagnose THIS iteration's `./trajectories/` ONLY (not stale signatures). Cluster ALL
   failures by shared root cause — total, partial-credit, AND communication/omission.
   RANK clusters by LEVERAGE = (# failing tasks × trials × score recoverable), biggest
   first — but plan to fix ALL of them this iteration, not only the top few.
3. For EACH cluster, pick the strongest improvement TYPE from `./guidance/tools/SKILL.md`
   (cross-check the FAILURE TYPE section next) and draft the edit. Across the iteration use
   MULTIPLE different types, not the same one repeatedly. Run each edit through the THREE
   TESTS; keep it only if it passes all three.
4. Ship every passing edit together in this ONE candidate — cover as many clusters as you
   can SAFELY (that is the win), and never include an edit that fails a test.
5. Fill `PROCESS.md` and APPEND your entry to `JOURNAL.md`. STOP.

## Choose the lever by FAILURE TYPE
Every lever below is a change to `tools/tools.py`. There is no prompt to edit.

- **RULE VIOLATION** — the agent breaks a policy rule, precondition or formula it could
  already follow. **Default strong lever: move the rule INTO THE CODE BODY of the EXISTING
  tool that governs it** — an in-body validation / normalization / computation that raises
  an ACTIONABLE error or returns the corrected value, scoped to fire ONLY on the violating
  condition. Highest yield, lowest regression; reach for it first. *Example:*
  ```
  def book_reservation(..., payment_methods):
  +   on_file = set(self._get_user(user_id).payment_methods)
  +   bad = [p["payment_id"] for p in payment_methods if p["payment_id"] not in on_file]
  +   if bad:                                          # fires only on the violation
  +       raise ValueError(f"payment_id(s) {bad} not on the user's profile; "
  +                        f"available={sorted(on_file)}")
      ...
  ```
- **CAPABILITY GAP / ACTION STALL** — the agent has NO reliable way to do the thing (a
  hard-ZERO cluster needing a real compute / composite / discriminating-predicate tool), or
  it narrates a multi-step action then never executes it. **Documentation does NOTHING for
  a hard zero** — a 0.00 task stays 0.00 after any docstring reword; it needs a TOOL the
  agent will CALL that changes the graded state. ADD a NEW code-bearing tool that closes
  the gap — a composite atomic-WRITE tool whose body performs the whole action via the
  existing primitives (then add the raw primitives to `REMOVE_TOOLS` so the action cannot
  be skipped), or a loop / validation tool. Add a tool ONLY when it closes a real gap AND
  the agent will call it AND it changes the graded outcome — NOT a read/compute/summary
  helper a guard would subsume, and never to hit a quota.
- **KNOWLEDGE GAP** — a format, criterion or fact the agent genuinely cannot derive → a
  precise docstring rule on the tool that needs it. Don't restate a rule the agent already
  has; that's a rule-violation (use code), not a knowledge gap.
- **DECISION / PERMISSION (ACT vs REFUSE)** — the agent made the wrong call on a decision
  the policy governs: it ACTED where it should have refused/escalated (or the reverse).
  **This is the most dangerous cluster to fix wrong.** NEVER widen or remove a refusal a
  tool already performs to fix it: that flips behavior for the WHOLE class and regresses
  every currently-passing task where the stricter behavior was the gold answer (this exact
  mistake sank a prior run). Instead encode the EXACT discriminating CONDITION in an
  in-body guard on the tool that owns the action, which refuses/raises ONLY when the
  precise policy predicate is/isn't met — bounded blast radius: only the qualifying cases
  change. The policy the agent is held to is in the benchmark source; read it there rather
  than inferring the predicate from one trace.

Also improve **tool RETURN values / error messages** (actionable: what's wrong + the valid
options + the next step) when a recoverable error stranded the agent — high-leverage and
low-risk, because the return value is what steers the agent's NEXT turn.

## VERIFY-THE-FIX (do this for EACH kept edit — it satisfies the VERIFIED + SAFE tests)
Your tool code is importable and the airline database loads offline, so you can execute a
tool body directly instead of reasoning about it. Do that:
```
from tau2.domains.airline.data_model import FlightDB
from tau2.domains.airline.utils import AIRLINE_DB_PATH
import importlib.util; s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("t", "tools/tools.py")
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m)
tools = m.AirlineTools(FlightDB.load(AIRLINE_DB_PATH))   # pristine state, as each rollout gets
```
- **In-body guard / computation:** run the tool on the EXACT args from the failing trace and
  confirm it fires / returns the corrected value. THEN run it on the args from 1–2
  currently-PASSING tasks that use the same tool and confirm it does NOT fire (the
  blast-radius / SAFE check). A guard that never fires on the failing task is dead code;
  one that fires on a passing task is a regression — rescope or drop it.
- **Decision / permission edit:** the SAFE check is BEHAVIORAL. Enumerate the
  currently-passing tasks in the SAME decision class and confirm the edit would not flip
  the agent's action on any of them — in particular that it does not make the agent newly
  ACT where a passing task's gold answer was to refuse or escalate.
- **New tool:** construct the inputs the agent SHOULD have passed (from the trace's observed
  state) and run the body; confirm it completes the action end-to-end and that
  `AirlineTools(...).get_tools()` still returns a schema for every exposed tool.
- **Removed tool:** confirm no currently-passing task's trace depends on the removed
  primitive, and that the composite that replaces it covers every use those traces show.
- **Docstring:** confirm the missing fact is now stated, general, and unambiguous.

Record one line per edit in PROCESS.md, e.g.
`trace <task> arg payment_id=<bad> → guard raises "<msg>"; passing tasks <ids> → does NOT fire`.
An edit with no verification line is unverified — verify it or drop it.

## NON-OVERFITTING (every edit must GENERALIZE)
Every edit encodes a GENERAL rule that holds across the whole class of inputs — NEVER a
literal that special-cases one task (its id, user, reservation, flight number, or expected
answer). A guard fires on the general condition ("the payment id is not on the user's
profile", "the reservation is in a state that forbids this change"), NOT
`if reservation_id == "<TASK_SPECIFIC_ID>"`. ALLOWED: constants the airline policy or the
data model defines (the policy's stated current date, the fixed baggage/cabin fees, a
domain enum). Use per-task specifics and any ground truth visible in `reward_info` ONLY to
understand the failure CLASS, then write the general fix.

## Handover (REQUIRED before you STOP)
- **PROCESS.md** (this iteration): the ranked cluster list (with leverage + RULE/GAP/
  KNOWLEDGE/DECISION tag), every kept edit + its lever, the VERIFY-THE-FIX + blast-radius
  line per edit, what you deliberately skipped and why, and (if you used subagents) that
  you did.
- **JOURNAL.md** (append ONE entry below the marker; never edit earlier entries). Write
  INTENT only — you cannot know your gate result; the framework stamps the RESULT below
  your entry: the changes I made (1 line/edit, naming the tool + cluster) · the EXPECTED
  effect + why each is safe · which prior RESULTS I built on and which regressing edits I
  did NOT re-try (cite ids) · refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT disproved — never
  re-test) · high-value clusters not yet cracked + designs already tried · plateau signal +
  which lever to switch to · focus next iteration.

These tasks already score ~1.0. Preserve their behavior: any edit that changes their trajectory is a regression and will be rejected. Protect: 19

## What you are editing (the allowed edit space)
The capability under optimization is composed of these editable artifact(s). Use the FULL edit space below — do not limit yourself to trivial wording tweaks.
- **tools** — Optimize an agent's own tool surface — docs, parameter schema/API, tool code, composing tools that call existing tools, adding/removing tools.
  - Allowed edits: Edit tool names/descriptions, per-parameter docs, in-description examples, the JSON schema, and the handler code. HIGHEST-LEVERAGE EDIT: WRITE A NEW CODE-BEARING TOOL (a real body — loops, validation, calls to existing tools), because a deterministic tool can't be 'forgotten' the way a prompt rule can. Two patterns to prefer: (1) a VALIDATION/RULE-ENFORCEMENT tool that wraps a primitive — validate/normalize inputs, enforce a GENERAL rule, then delegate to the primitive (e.g. cancel_record_safely(id) checks cancellable then calls cancel_record), and REMOVE the raw primitive so the only path is the safe one; (2) a WORKFLOW/LOOP tool that collapses a recurring multi-step sequence or N repeated calls into ONE call with real loops (e.g. loop get_record over a list of ids). Keep the toolset LEAN — REPLACE/consolidate, don't accumulate. The body must be real code, never '...' or docstring-only. Selection is driven by the name+description; argument-filling by the parameter schema/enums.
  - Full guidance (read it): ./guidance/tools/SKILL.md
## How your edit is judged
Algorithm: hill-climb:all. Your edited candidate is re-scored on the SAME held-out val tasks and compared to the current best (val reward 0.400). It is ACCEPTED only if the per-task improvement clears a significance bar (a noise margin), so a tiny or lucky change is rejected. Aim for a real, generalizing gain across a CLASS of failures — not a one-off patch to a single task (that overfits and gets rejected or hurts the held-out test).

## Self-check before STOP
- Every kept edit passes the THREE TESTS (REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED) and has its verify +
  blast-radius line in PROCESS.md. Drop any that doesn't.
- You read `./guidance/tools/SKILL.md` and applied MULTIPLE DIFFERENT improvement types it
  describes (not the same lever repeated), and you read
  `./guidance/sources/data_model.py` before writing code against those types.
- You addressed EVERY failing cluster you found this iteration (not just the top few), and
  did NOT defer a capability-gap cluster to "next iteration" — you built the tool now.
- Your `tools/tools.py` diff contains real CODE (in-body guards / validations / new or
  changed tool bodies / a composite tool) across SEVERAL tools — NOT just docstring text.
  If the only change is documentation, you under-used the iteration: convert the
  behavioral / rule-violation / capability-gap clusters into code and try again.
- Every BEHAVIORAL cluster (the agent knows the rule but skips the action) is fixed in
  CODE, not by another docstring line it will skim the same way.
- You did NOT try to edit the system prompt / airline policy — it is not part of this
  capability and no such file is yours to change.
- For DECISION / PERMISSION clusters you did NOT widen or remove a refusal a tool already
  performs; you encoded the discriminating CONDITION and confirmed it does not flip the
  action on any passing task in the class.
- For any hard-ZERO cluster you shipped a real tool the agent will call (documentation does
  nothing for a zero).
- Any new tool closes a real gap, will be called, and changes the graded outcome — not a
  helper a guard subsumes, not quota-filling. Every exposed tool still yields a schema.
- No edit hardcodes a task-specific id/value/date/answer.
- PROCESS.md + JOURNAL.md are filled. Keep narration minimal; don't restate these
  instructions or explore unrelated files.


## Run budget — THIS MAY BE YOUR LAST ITERATION (iteration 1/1 (0 after this one); 0/1 consecutive rejects)
Update `META_INSIGHTS.md` and `FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md` THIS iteration — there may be no next one to do it in.

## Cross-iteration files in THIS working dir (clean ownership — read all)
- `LEDGER.md` — FACTS (framework, read-only): every iteration's outcome + the tasks it MEASURABLY broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was under 2·SE and so resolves nothing. Never re-introduce a change that broke a task; never redesign an edit because a task landed in `unresolved`.
- `JOURNAL.md` — HANDOVER (yours, append-only across the whole run): read the whole thing, then APPEND your entry for this iteration below the marker line. Do NOT edit earlier entries. This is how you avoid repeating refuted ideas and hitting the same plateau.
- `PROCESS.md` — EXPLAINABILITY (yours, REQUIRED this iteration): fill it in as you work (ranked issues, every edit + class, verify-the-fix, subagents/features used, what to preserve, what you skipped). It is snapshotted with your candidate.
- `RUNMAP.md` + `./prior_iterations/<id>/` — every prior iteration's PROCESS.md + capability diff, copied in for you. Read the ones targeting your cluster BEFORE proposing, so you build on prior work instead of repeating it.
- `INSIGHTS.md` — SUMMARIZED, VERIFIED findings (yours, append-only, optional most iterations): a distilled 'what worked / what didn't / what's promising' a future iteration reads INSTEAD of the whole journal. Add an entry whenever you have a new CONFIRMED finding (cite the RESULT that confirmed it).
